summary:
Verified on the current build. The reviewer's core thesis holds. The 104 files are cleanly mastered and the .m4a fallback, fog gating and calm/combat layer work, but VALE's audio is a shared generic library and not yet a MOBA soundscape. Of 9 blockers and majors, I confirmed 5, downgraded 4 and refuted none.

Confirmed:
- AUD-2 (blocker): the queue pop is digital silence in a hidden tab at default settings. Re-captured in harness Chrome: post-limiter output has no non-zero sample and master gain is 0.0. With only muteInBackground switched off, the same play peaks at -8.2 dBFS.
- AUD-5, AUD-6, AUD-8, AUD-9 (major).

Downgraded:
- AUD-1 to major: the r12 visual twin M12 is rated major, and CONTRACT §11 scopes out voice.
- AUD-3 to minor: no spoken announcer is a documented choice (CONTRACT §11: tonal, no voice in this slice, subtitles carry the text), and the HUD banners name every event.
- AUD-4 to minor: the numbers reproduce, but the crit is brighter, not darker; magic hits are bright; and r07 marks the three-layer impact as an unverified craft norm.
- AUD-7 to minor: the measured harm is small. There were 2 of 6,344 blocks over 0 dBFS, and -20.7 LUFS is measured at the default master of 0.8.

Missed blocker-class bug: the audio engine plays enemy-team pings and enemy surrender votes for you, which the HUD deliberately hides. I reproduced this in a live match. Online lockstep applies every seat's commands, so in PvP this leaks the enemy team's communications.

Also missed (minor): the 'On my way' ping is always silent. content/audio.json:110 binds 'ping.onmyway', but the PingKind is 'onMyWay' (src/contracts/sim.ts:60), so src/audio/index.ts:439 finds no cue.

gapStatus: the r12 gaps M2, M5, M6, M12, M13, M14 and m2 are visual by definition, and r12 says sound was not studied. They are set to not_measured, with the audio analogue given in the evidence.

New artifacts:
- _harness/_reports/final_audio_verify_files.json
- _harness/_reports/final_audio_verify_qpop.json
- _harness/_reports/final_audio_verify_enemy_ping.json

gapStatus.evidence:
r12 M12 is a visual gap: VFX signature hue and teamTint. r12 §1 says 'Sound was not studied'. This audio review did not measure the visual facet.

Audio analogue, still open (AUD-1, re-verified with the scratchpad script kits.py over content/fighters/*.json): 16 kits use 27 distinct cues, and none was authored for a single fighter. The 4 single-user cues (c_blink, c_hit_true, c_shot_bow, c_crit) are generic event cues. No cue in content/audio.json has more than one file.

r12 M13 is the visual exposure envelope of ultimates, which was not measured here.

Audio analogue, still open: c_ult_windup is the ult present.sfx in 14/16 kits, and c_ult_windup plus c_ult_release appear together in 12/16 (_harness/_reports/final_audio_kit_identity.txt, re-derived).

r12 M2 covers status VFX and status words, which were not measured here.

Audio analogue, still open (AUD-5): content/audio.json binds only status.stun, status.root and status.slow. Every other status falls back to c_buff (src/audio/index.ts:408-411): fear, sleep, airborne, taunt, disarm, silence, haste and the shreds.

r12 M5 covers attack timing, trails and hit VFX, which were not measured here.

Audio analogue, a minor gap (AUD-4): physical hit cues carry less than 2% of their first-30 ms energy above 2 kHz. A 220 Hz laptop roll-off costs them 4.2-4.8 LU, against 1.4 LU for the calm bed (_harness/_reports/final_audio_verify_files.json).

r12 M6 is the victim hit-flash, which was not measured here.

Audio facet: every attack and ability damage event has a hit cue (src/audio/index.ts:391-405). Exception: passive damage without a delivery emits only 'damage' with ability set, which index.ts:402 skips (see AUD-6).

r12 M14 is visual ambient life, which was not measured here.

Audio analogue, still open (AUD-8):
- 0 of 94 cues use the 'ambience' bus. The counts are sfx 49, ui 32, voice 10, music 3.
- content/maps/map_{rift,bridge,fray}.json contain 0 sfx, audio or ambience keys.
- The Settings ambience slider (src/ui/screens/settings.tsx:147) drives an empty bus.

findings.title: Fighters have no audio identity: a shared 27-cue library, near-identical ults, autos shared with Wicks and camp monsters, one file per cue
findings.what:
All 16 kits pick from one generic combat library, and nothing is authored per fighter.
- 12/16 ultimates use the same wind-up and release pair.
- 11 of 16 fighters' basic attacks use exactly the (swing, hit) cue pair of a Wick or a camp monster. The reviewer counted 8: 8 match a Wick and 3 more match Gloamoth or Sunsplinter. Only the level differs: fighters play at gain 0.6/0.8, units at 0.3/0.45 (src/audio/index.ts:397, :404).
- Every cue is a single file with no round-robin. Cues do carry a ±2-10% playback-rate pitch variation (pitchVar 0.02-0.10).
- Projectiles, dashes, heals and shields always use one generic cue.
- There is no fighter voice, and draft lock-in plays the same 'lockin' for every fighter (src/ui/screens/draft.tsx:162, :322).
findings.evidence:
Re-derived independently with the scratchpad script kits.py over content/fighters/*.json and content/units.json:
- 16 fighters use 27 distinct cues.
- The only single-user cues are c_blink (dunsom), c_hit_true (kemdo), c_shot_bow (lisvel) and c_crit (rishal), all generic event cues.
- c_ult_windup is the ult present.sfx in 14 of 16 kits.

Attack pairs shared with units:
- (c_swing_heavy, c_hit_phys_heavy): burdam, ervet, hesmi, kemdo and marund, plus brightwick.
- (c_swing_light, c_hit_phys_light): ardit, nurrow and rishal, plus shieldwick.
- (c_shot_bolt_lumen, c_hit_magic): ilsheta, sukri and vashil, plus gloamoth and sunsplinter.

In content/audio.json, 0 of 94 cues have more than one file.

Capture (_harness/_reports/final_audio_mix_summary.json): c_hit_phys_light played 2,261 times in 541 s. The audio/build.py variants machinery exists (cuelib.py:33, build.py:132), but every cue uses variants=1.
findings.gauge: In LoL each champion has its own auto-attack, cast, impact and ultimate sounds and its own VO. The LoL wiki Quote page gives minimum line counts per champion. r07 [39] describes champion SFX as a trade-off between clarity and character. A LoL player hears who cast what, including off-screen.
findings.files: content/fighters/*.json, content/audio.json, audio/cues/kit.py, audio/cues/combat.py, audio/build.py, src/ui/screens/draft.tsx
findings.verifierNote:
Reproduced. Every count matches, except that the minion/monster overlap is 11 fighters, not 8.

Downgraded from blocker to major:
1. r12 rates the visual equivalent, M12 ('fighters cannot be told apart by their effects'), as major.
2. The shared impact set is the CONTRACT §11 spec ('impact set (attack light/heavy, ability hit by damage type, crit ...)'), and voice is explicitly out of this slice.
3. Nothing is broken or unfair: abilities are partly distinguished by 27 cues in lumen and shade families.

The parity gap is still large (XL) and is the main reason the score stays low.

findings.title: The queue pop is silent in a background tab at default settings
findings.what:
A player who queues and switches tabs hears nothing when the match is found.
- muteInBackground defaults to true and sets the master gain to 0 while hidden.
- ui_queue_pop is an ordinary UI cue behind that master and has no bypass.
- There is no Notification API or favicon fallback. Only a title flash remains, so the 10 s ready check is easy to miss.
- A miss costs an escalating lockout (5 s up to 60 s). Online, it also sends the other humans back (server/room.ts ready check).
findings.evidence:
Reproduced in harness Chrome, writing _harness/_reports/final_audio_verify_qpop.json:
- Phase A: tab hidden (document.hidden and visibilityState overridden, visibilitychange dispatched), default settings, queue found. ui_queue_pop is in the cue log, yet the post-limiter output has no non-zero sample over 72 blocks (3.0 s) and master gain is 0.0 throughout.
- Phase B: same hidden tab, only muteInBackground switched off via session.updateSettings, then the same 'queue_pop' role. Output peaks at -8.2 dBFS with master gain 0.8.

Code:
- src/session/settings.ts:52 sets muteInBackground: true.
- src/audio/index.ts:139-143: applyVolumes sets master to 0 while hidden.
- src/ui/state.ts:158 plays the pop; :161 is a title flash only.
- No Notification usage anywhere in src.
- _design/tokens.json:446 queuePop.ownSliderWithFloor is unimplemented.

Repro:
```
node <scratchpad>/audio/qpop.mjs _harness/_reports/final_audio_verify_qpop.json
```
findings.gauge: r07 §3.3 calls match-found the highest-stakes sound in the product. LoL's ready check is about 12 s, and missing it costs the lobby. The FACEIT precedent (verified in r07 [55]) plays it while tabbed out or minimized, on by default. r07 §7 item 7 asks for Notification, tab-title and favicon redundancy.
findings.fix:
Route the gate cues (ui_queue_pop, a ready reminder, m_countdown, m_match_start) on an 'alert' bus connected to the limiter after the background-mute gain. Give that bus a floor the UI slider cannot go below, which implements the tokens rule ownSliderWithFloor.

If the player has not accepted with 4 s left, play a softer two-pulse hourbell reminder.

Ask for Notification permission on the first queue, and add a favicon badge next to the title flash.

Keep muteInBackground for everything else.
findings.verifierNote:
Reproduced with a control. Background mute is the sole cause: the same play is -8.2 dBFS once muteInBackground is off.

Correction: VALE's ready check is 10 s (src/session/matchmaker.ts:17, server/room.ts:48), not about 12 s; the 12 s figure is LoL's.

Offline searches last only 2-6 s (matchmaker.ts:18), so the case mainly bites online queues, where waits are real and a miss hurts other humans.

Blocker is kept: the client's single most important gate sound fails silently in the common tabbed-out case at default settings, against an explicit r07 requirement, and the fix is small.

findings.title: Announcer stings do not distinguish events and stack in the same tick, with no queue
findings.what:
The engine sorts every announcement into 'major' or 'minor' with a regex.
- A 5-fighter multi-takedown, a shutdown and a failed surrender all play the same 0.81 s minor sting.
- Structure and objective falls emit two events in the same tick, so two voice-bus stings play at once.
- There is no one-at-a-time queue, no merging and no expiry.

The information itself is not lost: the HUD banner names every event, including each multikill tier, shutdowns and a derived team wipe.
findings.evidence:
Code:
- src/audio/index.ts:441-444: /first|ace|objective|structure|inhib|core/ maps to m_announce_major, everything else to m_announce_minor.
- Same-tick pairs:
  - src/sim/units/structures.ts:148-149 emits 'structure', then announce structure_destroyed;
  - src/sim/units/monsters.ts:166-167 emits 'objective', then announce objective_taken;
  - src/sim/modes/match.ts:84 emits announce match_start, while the engine plays m_match_start at t=0 (index.ts:457).

In the capture, final_audio_mix_summary.json voice_stacks lists 4 of 6 announcer moments as double stings.

The HUD shows specific banners for every key: src/ui/hud/model.ts:492-560, with multikill tiers at :501-505 and the team wipe at :485-488.
findings.gauge: LoL speaks a distinct announcer line for each event class and schedules lines one at a time in sync with the banner (r07 §2.1-2.2).
findings.verifierNote:
The code and the capture reproduce, but this is downgraded to minor.

The headline claim (no spoken announcer) is a documented design choice:
- CONTRACT §11 (_spec/CONTRACT.md:791-792): 'announcer stingers (tonal, no voice in this slice; subtitles carry the text)';
- DESIGN_NOTE: 'The announcer is tonal with on-screen text'.

The HUD banners carry the exact event, and the reviewer's 'no team-wipe event exists' holds only for audio, since the HUD derives one (model.ts:485-488).

What remains is real but minor: undifferentiated stings, and same-tick double stings measured at -13 LUFS M_max.

findings.title: Physical hits, slam, stun and root have little high-frequency attack and lose 3-6 LU on a laptop roll-off
findings.what:
The physical hit family, plus c_slam, c_stun and c_root, has almost no energy above 2 kHz at the attack, and its centroid sits near 190-220 Hz. On a small speaker these cues thin out more than the music does.

It is not true that 'a hit never audibly connects'. Every hit reaches -6 dB within 5.3-7.8 ms of onset, on a 470 Hz knock for the light hit.

It is also not true that the crit is darker:
- c_crit's centroid is 388 Hz, against 185-191 Hz for the hits;
- its HF share is about twice theirs.

Magic hits (c_hit_magic, 747 plays) are bright and lose nothing on a laptop.
findings.evidence:
Independent re-measure of the shipped .ogg files (scratchpad verify_files.py, written to _harness/_reports/final_audio_verify_files.json). Columns are: >2 kHz share in the first 30 ms after a -40 dB onset (rectangular window) / loss through a 4th-order 220 Hz high-pass / loss through a 2nd-order 150 Hz high-pass.
- c_hit_phys_light: 0.018 / 4.8 / 1.9 LU
- c_hit_phys_heavy: 0.018 / 4.2 / 2.4
- c_crit: 0.039 / 3.7 / 2.5
- c_slam: 0.009 / 5.8 / 3.7
- c_stun: 0.007 / 3.0 / 1.9
- c_root: 0.001 / 2.7 / 1.7
- c_hit_magic: 0.246 / 0.1 / 0.0

The calm match bed mus_match_rift loses 1.4 LU through the same 220 Hz filter, and the intense layer loses 3.5 LU (scratchpad music_loss.py).

The reviewer's 1/3-octave distances (final_audio_confusable_pairs.json) are whole-file averages: they ignore c_stun's 8.5 Hz B5/F5 daze wobble and c_root's creak train (audio/cues/combat.py:487-541).
findings.gauge: r07 §3.1 recommends a three-layer impact with a bright 0-30 ms transient, and a crit that is 'the same hit, but sharper'. r07 labels this '[unverified as any studio's documented practice]', so it is a craft norm rather than a measured LoL number.
findings.fix:
Add a 0-30 ms 2-6 kHz transient layer (an escapement tick or glass snap) to c_hit_phys_light and c_hit_phys_heavy, at about 10-20% of the first-30 ms energy, while keeping the documented soft top on frequent cues.

Add a 300-800 Hz harmonic to c_slam and c_monster_hit, so a 220 Hz roll-off costs at most 3 LU.

Add build.py QA gates on the transient HF share and the laptop loss for c_hit_*, c_crit and the status cues.
findings.verifierNote:
The numbers reproduce within measurement-window differences (the reviewer used a Hanning window and a -30 dB onset).

Downgraded to minor:
1. The crit claim is contradicted by its own centroid and HF data.
2. Magic hits are bright.
3. The hits are tightly front-loaded.
4. On a laptop the hit-to-music margin shrinks by about 3.4 LU from a +6.3 dB median, which still leaves the hits above the music.
5. The gauge is an unverified craft norm, and the soft top on frequent cues is a documented anti-fatigue choice (audio/cues/combat.py header).

The CC-versus-hit separation is covered under AUD-5.

findings.title: Threat and CC are unreadable by ear: most hostile statuses play a friendly 'buff', and the enemy wind-up tell is limited and unpanned
findings.evidence:
- content/audio.json:103 binds only status.stun, status.root and status.slow. src/audio/index.ts:408-411 falls back to c_buff.
- Kit status uses, re-counted: slow 34, stun 9, root 9, haste 7, fear 6, sleep 6, airborne 4, taunt 3, disarm 3, silence 1.
- In the capture (final_audio_mix_summary.json), fear 25, airborne 65, disarm 25 and shred 200 applications were all voiced by c_buff (88 plays).
- c_buff takes 242 ms to reach -6 dB (final_audio_verify_files.json).
- src/audio/index.ts:387: the cue fires only when an enemy's slot is 'ult' within 14 m, with pos null.
- _design/STYLE_BIBLE.md:123: 'enemy T3+ wind-ups share one shade-breath swell'.
findings.gauge: r07 §0.3, §3.1 and §4.5 rank threat above self above ally, call the enemy wind-up the most important counterplay sound, and say hard CC must out-read damage. LoL players react to an enemy cast sound before the effect lands.
findings.verifierNote:
Reproduced from code, content and file measurements. Major is kept: a hostile fear, sleep or taunt on you sounds identical to an ally's haste.

Two small corrections:
- audio.json's $comment says the engine 'may' lift an enemy source by +1. That is a permission, not a promise.
- 'Hits blur with stun and root' is weaker than claimed (see AUD-4).

findings.title: Passive procs are silent: ~1,800 proc events per 9 minutes produce no sound, and 12/16 passives have no SFX
findings.what:
The sim emits a 'proc' event every time a passive triggers, but the audio engine has no handler for it. 12 of 16 passives also declare no sfx anywhere.

A passive's bonus damage that is not delivered by a projectile or area emits only a 'damage' event that carries the passive's ability id. The engine skips such events because 'ability hits voice through hit', and no 'hit' event is emitted for them.

The base attack's own hit still sounds. It is the payoff layer that both sides cannot hear.
findings.evidence:
- Capture (_harness/_reports/final_audio_mix_summary.json): 1,778 proc events.
- src/sim/triggers.ts:87-88 emits { e: 'proc', ... }. src/audio/index.ts:383-447 has no 'proc' case.
- Passive scan: ardit, burdam, dunsom, hesmi, ilsheta, kemdo, lisvel, marund, odrum, rishal, tunlan and vashil have no sfx. Ervet, nurrow, sukri and ulkro have some.
- src/sim/effects.ts:192 deals damage with ability = ctx.source.id. 'hit' is emitted only in onEffectHit (effects.ts:136-139, deliveries only). src/audio/index.ts:402 contains `if (e.ability) break;`.
findings.gauge: In LoL, passives that change a fight (empowered autos, mark detonations, stack payoffs) have their own proc sound, so both the user and the victim learn the timing.
findings.fix:
- Add case 'proc' in src/audio/index.ts. Play the passive's present.sfx at dst, or at src if there is no target, with a short per-fighter cooldown.
- Voice passive damage that has no delivery through the passive's hitSfx.
- Author the proc cues with each fighter kit (AUD-1).
- Add a content-build check: every passive with a damage, status, mark or resource payoff must declare a proc sfx.
findings.verifierNote: Reproduced. I also found the silent passive-damage path, which strengthens the finding. Major is kept, because a fight-relevant event class is entirely unhandled by the engine.

findings.title: The mixer limits only per cue: priority is unused, there is no voice-bus ducking or global budget, lifesteal chimes on every hit, and the limiter can overshoot
findings.evidence:
Code:
- src/audio/index.ts:252-257 steals only the same cue's oldest voice.
- priority is stored at :271 and never read, although the header at :5-6 claims a priority steal.
- duck() is called only from src/ui/state.ts:161.
- The compressor is set at index.ts:120-121.
- src/sim/combat.ts:133-135 calls heal() for vamp, and :161 emits 'heal'.

Capture (final_audio_mix_summary.json):
- c_heal 497 plays from 1,388 heal events;
- the post-limiter peak exceeded 0 dBFS in 2 of 6,344 blocks (max +0.25 dBFS) and -1 dBFS in 46;
- master integrated -20.7 LUFS at the default master of 0.8;
- SFX sat a median +6.3 dB over music.
findings.gauge: r07 §4.2-4.3 recommends a bus hierarchy with side-chain ducking, a global budget of about 32-48 voices ranked by priority × audibility, merging of ticks within 100 ms, and a -1 dBTP ceiling.
findings.fix:
- Implement the CONTRACT §11 ducking: under the voice bus, music -6 dB and SFX -3 dB.
- Add a global voice pool of about 32 ranked by priority × gain × attenuation, and use the priority field.
- Do not voice vamp heals, and merge heal ticks within 250 ms.
- Follow the compressor with a soft clip, or lower its threshold to -4 dB.

findings.title: The world is silent: no ambience on any map
findings.what: Outside combat the only sound is the music bed. There is no wind, water, lamp hum, crowd or structure presence, so jungle, river and base all sound the same. The Ambience slider controls nothing.
findings.evidence:
- Re-counted content/audio.json buses: sfx 49, ui 32, voice 10, music 3, ambience 0.
- content/maps/map_{rift,bridge,fray}.json contain 0 sfx, audio or ambience keys.
- src/ui/screens/settings.tsx:147 shows the ambience slider.
- Capture: master short-term p10 is -29.2 LUFS during laning, against a music-stem p50 of -28.8 (final_audio_mix_summary.json).
findings.gauge: r07 §1.3 describes Summoner's Rift as ambience plus a restrained reactive score. r07 §7 item 5 recommends an ambience-first match.
findings.verifierNote: Reproduced. Major is kept: the whole ambience layer that r07 recommends is absent, and a user-facing control drives nothing.

findings.title: The listener is your fighter (or your corpse), not the camera, against CONTRACT §11
findings.what:
Every spatial cue is attenuated and culled at 26 m from your fighter's position.

When you die, the camera goes free so you can watch the fight, but the listener stays at your corpse. A fight you spectate while dead, or watch with scout-hold, can therefore be silent.

In the default semi camera (6 m leash), an on-screen event near the screen edge plays up to about 11.5 dB down. Panning reaches ±0.85 by 12 m, and there is no distance filtering.
findings.evidence:
- src/audio/index.ts:50-51 (HEAR_M 26, NEAR_M 6), :243-250 (attenuation and pan dx/14 clamped to ±0.85) and :337-343 (youPos = your fighter entity, alive or not).
- src/sim/combat.ts:220-224: fighters stay in the store while dead.
- src/render/renderer.ts:946 calls rig.setSelf(null) when your fighter is dead, which makes the camera free (src/render/camera.ts:100).
- Default mode is 'semi' (camera.ts:25).
- CONTRACT §11 (_spec/CONTRACT.md:793-794): 'listener at the camera target'.
findings.gauge: r07 §4.4 recommends a hybrid listener at the camera's ground focus, plus an awareness pass near your fighter, and moderate panning of about ±60%. LoL players watch fights while dead or scouting. LoL's own listener placement is unverified (r07 §8 item 14).
findings.fix:
- Expose CameraRig.focus to the audio port and put the listener there, using 2D distance with an inner radius of about 12 m and a rolloff to about 30 m.
- Keep an awareness pass so enemy casts and attacks within 10 m of your living fighter stay audible.
- Pan at most ±0.6, with a gentle low-pass beyond 15 m.
findings.verifierNote:
Confirmed from code, and strengthened. The contract explicitly requires the camera target, and the dead-spectating case is real because the camera frees itself on death (renderer.ts:946).

In normal alive play the divergence is bounded by the 6 m leash.

The reviewer's capture never sampled a dead state (deadProbe dead 0), so this verdict rests on code. Major is kept because it is a contract deviation with a common failure case.

findings.title: Dead air before cues tied to instant events
findings.evidence:
Re-measured in _harness/_reports/final_audio_verify_files.json. Values are the first sample above -40 dB / -20 dB / -6 dB, then the peak:
- m_level_up: 118.8 / 125.2 / 126.0 / 268 ms
- m_respawn: 127 / 464 / 506 / 518 ms
- c_blink: 51 / 112 / 160 / 186 ms
- c_summon: 72 / 233 / 306 / 310 ms
- m_ping_vision: 105 / 171 / 196 / 199 ms
findings.gauge: Cues for instant events land on the event frame, and swells are reserved for deliberate wind-ups.
findings.fix: Trim the pre-roll so the first -20 dB sample comes within 15 ms for instant events (blink, level-up, respawn, summon, pings). Add a build.py gate keyed on an 'instant' recipe flag.
findings.verifierNote: Reproduced within 1-3 ms of the reviewer's values.

findings.title: The music is static: one 160 s match loop with one layer, a 96 s menu file, and a draft bed blind to the draft
findings.what:
- The match bed is a single 160 s loop with one 'intense' layer, so it repeats about 11 times in a 30-minute match.
- The menu bed is one 96 s file, although the tokens specify stems [64, 48, 80] with a 960 s full repeat.
- The draft bed is a linear 136 s file, with no phase sync and no 8 s urgency layer for the local player.
findings.evidence:
- ffprobe: mus_match_* and their *_intense layers are 160.0 s, mus_menu 96.0 s, mus_draft 136.0 s, mus_postgame 80.0 s.
- _design/tokens.json:463-464 specifies the menu stems and the draft phases with localUrgencyLastS 8.
- src/ui/screens/draft.tsx plays only lockin and ban.
findings.gauge: r07 §1.2-1.3: draft music builds toward lock-in, and the match score reacts to game progress and location while staying in the background.
findings.fix:
- Render the menu as the three tokens stems, looped independently.
- Give the draft phase layers driven by draft state, plus a local 8 s urgency pulse.
- Later, add dead and objective match states (r07 §7 item 5).
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed. Note that the tokens specify only calm and combat for the match (tokens.json:465), so the dead, objective and late states are r07 recommendations beyond the spec.

findings.title: .m4a fallback beds decode several times slower in Safari, and the bed waits for both stems
findings.what: On a browser that falls back to .m4a, match music can start many seconds late, because startBed waits for the main stem and the layer together (Promise.all). Safari 27 decodes .ogg, so the problem is latent.
findings.evidence:
- _harness/_reports/final_audio_probe_safari_layer.json (today): mus_match_rift_intense decodes as .m4a in 20,946 ms vs .ogg in 2,040 ms.
- The mus_menu figures of 5,302 / 2,127 ms are in _harness/_reports/audio_probe_safari.json. final_audio_probe_safari.json actually holds a 2026-10-20 run (2,855 / 1,463 ms).
- src/audio/index.ts:301 uses Promise.all.
findings.gauge: LoL's client starts its music immediately on every supported platform.
findings.fix: Start the main stem as soon as it decodes, and fade the layer in on the next bar once it is ready. On the .m4a path, decode beds as 16 s segments.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed, with a citation correction. The '10x' slowdown comes from the single layer sample; the menu bed shows 2-2.5x.

findings.title: Audio accessibility is thin: no mono or loud-transient option, and the ambience slider does nothing
findings.what:
Settings offer six sliders and a background-mute toggle. There is no mono mix and no option to reduce loud transients, and the ambience slider drives an empty bus.

The subtitles toggle does work: it shows or hides the announcer banner, which CONTRACT §11 names as the tonal announcer's subtitles.
findings.evidence:
- src/ui/screens/settings.tsx:147-159 holds the sliders and muteInBackground.
- Subtitles toggle at :310-311, consumed by src/ui/hud/top.tsx:133.
- The ambience bus has 0 cues.
- r07 §5 items 4 and 6.
findings.gauge: r07 §5 and the Game Accessibility Guidelines [49] ask for separate speech, effects and music controls, a mono option, and no essential information carried by sound alone.

BLOCKER-CLASS (competitive integrity, size S): the audio engine plays the ENEMY team's pings and surrender votes for you, which the HUD deliberately hides.

Reproduced in a live RIFT co-op match (_harness/_reports/final_audio_verify_enemy_ping.json; you = seat 8, team 1). A 'danger' ping and a 'missing' ping issued through the sim by enemy seat 0 (team 0) each played their cue for you: m_ping_danger, then m_ping_missing.

Cause:
- src/ui/hud/model.ts:431 drops other-team pings (`pv.team !== this.myTeam`), but src/audio/index.ts:439 plays every ping with no team check.
- Likewise, model.ts:547 and :556 ignore the other team's surrender_vote and surrender_failed, but index.ts:441-444 plays m_announce_minor for every announce key.
- Online PvP is lockstep and every client applies every seat's commands (src/session/lockstep_host.ts:165), so each player hears the kind and timing of every enemy ping (danger, missing, objective, push, retreat ...) and every enemy surrender vote.

In LoL, pings and surrender votes are team-private.

Fix: gate 'ping' on view.players[e.player].team === myTeam, and gate the team-private announce keys (surrender_*) on e.team === myTeam, plus a regression test.

Repro:
```
node <scratchpad>/audio/enemyping.mjs _harness/_reports/final_audio_verify_enemy_ping.json
```
